title: Moon-forming giant impact
summary: About 4.5 billion years ago a Mars-sized body, named Theia, is thought to have struck the early Earth, and the debris it threw out formed the Moon. The idea explains the Moon's molten early state and its chemical similarity to Earth, though details such as the impact angle remain debated.

uncertainty.note: NASA gives only "about 4.5 billion years ago"; the year -4,510,000,000 follows the atlas id and the plus/minus is a rounding bracket. NASA also says about 60 million years after the solar system began forming; Astronomy magazine says when the solar system was about 50 million years old.

as_recorded.value: when the solar system was about 50 million years old

where.modern_name: Early Earth (no surface location; planetary-scale event)
where.historical_name: Hadean Earth, before any continents or polities

importance.justification: The leading explanation for the origin of the Moon, which shapes Earth tides, spin and later history.

sources.title: Theia slammed into Earth, left marks and then formed the Moon, study suggests
sources.author: Astronomy magazine

reviewer_note: Coordinates 0,0 are a placeholder for a planet-scale event; the coordinate source is the NASA page only in the sense that it describes a whole-Earth event. The 4.51 Ga year follows the id, while sources give only about 4.5 Ga. Confidence is probable: it is the leading hypothesis, not settled.
